title: O, Send Me Not Away! for I Would Drink
description: O, Send Me Not Away! for I Would Drink in Tonic Solfa to LANGRAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 202, “The Broken Shield”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10) (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LANGRAN; any other Tens (10.10.10.10) tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, send me not a-way! for I would drink, Even I, the weak-est, at the fount of life; Chide not my steps, that ven-ture near the brink, Wea-ry and faint-ing from the dead-ly strife.

lines: O, send me not away! for I would drink,
Even I, the weakest, at the fount of life;
Chide not my steps, that venture near the brink,
Weary and fainting from the deadly strife.
Went I not forth undaunted and alone,
Strong in the majesty of human might?
Lo! I return, all wounded and forlorn,
My dream of glory lost in shades of night.
Was I not girded for the battle-field?
Bore I not helm of pride and glittering sword?
Behold the fragments of my broken shield,
And lend to me Thy heavenly armor, Lord!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to LANGRAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
